subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: A random variable X has the following probability distribution: X = −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3; P(X = x) = 0.1, k, 0.2, 2k, 0.3, k. Find k and the variance of X.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find k and the variance from this table — what equation gives k, why you still need the mean, and what you square in the variance formula.
insider_note: The question never mentions the mean, but two of the seven marks are for finding it — the variance formula subtracts μ² = 0.64; keep the minus signs on the −2 and −1 rows, since they disappear only when the values are squared.

steps.label: Find k
steps.margin_note: First two marks. The table mixes decimals and k's. Add the decimals (0.1 + 0.2 + 0.3 = 0.6) and the k's (k + 2k + k = 4k) separately, set 4k + 0.6 = 1, and k = 0.1. Work in decimals throughout — the whole table is in decimals.

recall.must_convey: That the probabilities add to 1, so 4k + 0.6 = 1 and k = 0.1.
accept: the probabilities add to one so four k plus point six is one and k is point one
sum of P equals one gives four k equals point four so k is point one
add the decimals and the k terms, set equal to one, k comes to zero point one
anni probabilities kalipithe one, four k plus point six equals one, k point one
use sigma P equals one and k is one by ten

steps.why: The probabilities must add to 1 because X takes exactly one of the six values in every trial. Nothing else in the table fixes k.
common_mistakes: Adding the x-values (−2 − 1 + 0 + 1 + 2 + 3) instead of the probabilities.

steps.label: Find the mean
steps.margin_note: Two marks, even though the question does not ask for the mean — the variance formula needs μ². Negative values give negative products: (−2)(0.1) = −0.2 and (−1)(k) = −k. Collect: 4k + 0.4 = 0.8.

recall.must_convey: That the mean is Σxᵢ·P(X = xᵢ) = 4k + 0.4 = 0.8, keeping the signs of −2 and −1.
accept: mean is sigma x times P of x which is four k plus point four equals point eight
multiply each value by its probability with the minus signs and add to get point eight
mu equals sum of x i P x i, comes to zero point eight
prathi x ni probability tho multiply chesi, minus signs tho add cheste mean point eight
the mean is four k plus point four which is point eight

steps.why: The mean is the weighted average of the values, and the variance formula subtracts its square — so the mean is a required step even when the question does not name it.
common_mistakes: Dropping the minus signs on −2 and −1.
Skipping the mean because the question asks only for the variance.

steps.label: Find the variance
steps.margin_note: Three marks. Square each value first — (−2)² = 4, (−1)² = 1, so every squared term is positive — multiply by its probability, add, then subtract μ² = 0.64. The k terms are k + 2k + 9k = 12k = 1.2.

recall.must_convey: That the variance is Σxᵢ²·P(X = xᵢ) − μ² = 2.8 − 0.64 = 2.16, with the values squared before multiplying.
accept: variance is sigma x squared P of x minus mu squared which is two point eight minus point six four equals two point one six
square each value times its probability, add, subtract the mean squared to get two point one six
sigma squared equals two point eight minus zero point six four
x square into probability add chesi mean square teesesthe variance two point one six
the variance comes to two point one six

steps.why: Squaring removes the signs, so negative values still increase the variance — a value at −2 is as far from the centre as one at +2. The formula Σxᵢ²P − μ² is quicker than Σ(xᵢ − μ)²P when μ is a decimal.
common_mistakes: Keeping the sign after squaring, writing (−2)² = −4.
Squaring the probabilities instead of the values.
